outcome: Neither Danzer's original problem (existence of a Danzer set of bounded density) nor Conway's dead fly variant (existence of a Danzer set of bounded separation) has been resolved, refuted, or seen a case settled since 26 January 2024; the only post-window arXiv paper found in this area addresses a distinct, weaker problem (low-visibility dense forests) rather than Danzer sets themselves.
summary: Danzer's 1965 problem (does a Danzer set of bounded density exist?) and Conway's 'dead fly' variant (does a Danzer set of bounded separation exist?) both remain open as of September 2026. The Wikipedia article on Danzer sets, fetched directly, states the core existence question is still unsolved and that known constructions (e.g. growth rate O(T^d log T) by Solomon and Weiss, predating the window) do not have bounded density. Conway's $1000 prize for the separation variant remains unclaimed. The triage record flagged arXiv:2407.01633 ('A New Construction of Forests with Low Visibility', posted July 2024, revised through v3 in December 2024) as a possible lead. I fetched both the abstract page and the PDF: the paper's abstract and visible text contain no mention of 'Danzer', 'Danzer set', or 'Danzer's problem' at all. It constructs a set of points of finite density in R^d such that every sufficiently long line segment comes within distance ε of a point of the set, using at most O(ε^-(d-1) ln ε^-1) points per unit length — an improvement to the 'low-visibility dense forest' bound (previously O(ε^-(d-1) log(ε^-1) log log(ε^-1)^(1+η)) by Tsokanos). A dense/optical forest of finite density with optimal visibility would itself be a Danzer set, but this paper's construction is explicitly a weakening (finite density but not proven optimal/universal visibility against all convex bodies of unit volume) and per the Wikipedia article's own framing, dense-forest work of this kind is a standard relaxation of Danzer's problem, not a case of it — changing the question (bounded visibility for line segments) rather than restricting it. Per DEEP_DIVE §3.1, this is a related problem, not a case of the stated problem, so it does not move the status. No search turned up any AI system credited with progress on Danzer sets, dense forests, or Conway's separation problem; the search results that surfaced 'AI + math problem' matches (DeepMind's FunSearch/cap-set result, Erdős-problems-site tooling) concern unrelated problems. I therefore classify this as open with no_change_found true, and no AI role.
competing_reading: One could argue that improving the dense-forest visibility bound is 'progress' worth recording as `progress` with `ai_role none`, since dense forests are the standard relaxation researchers use precisely because Danzer's problem itself resists direct attack, and any improvement there is the closest thing to forward motion on this cluster of questions in the window. However, per the scope rule in §3.1, a dense forest of finite density is not a Danzer set (it need not intersect every convex body of unit volume, only get close to long line segments), so a bound on it does not change what a careful person would write in the Danzer-set bullet itself. I did not find any source stating that 2407.01633's construction achieves the Danzer property (visibility of every convex body of unit volume rather than long line segments), so I did not upgrade to `progress`.
what_would_settle_it: A source (paper, survey, or updated Wikipedia article) explicitly stating either (a) a Danzer set of bounded density or bounded separation has been constructed or proven impossible, or (b) that a specific post-2024 dense-forest construction (such as 2407.01633) achieves the full Danzer property (finite density and universal visibility of every convex body of volume 1), which would make it a genuine case/instance of the problem rather than a related relaxation.
